ordered_diagnoses: Borderline personality disorder with psychotic features

support_spans: catatonia-like signs: flat affect with psychomotor retardation and fluctuating mutism; complete lack of social contact; twitching, eye grimacing, and shoulder shrugging; posturing and immobility; diaphoresis.

clues suggesting volitional behavior included selective acceptance of benzodiazepines and gabapentin while refusing other medications, eating all meals despite “stupor,” abruptly lapsing into and out of catatonia-like and psychotic behaviors depending on the topic of conversation, purposeful movements to obtain lorazepam after seizures
contradict_spans: A regional catatonia specialist evaluated her and noted that she was unlikely to have catatonia.
concepts.why: The patient's catatonia-like signs and psychotic signs, combined with clues suggesting volitional behavior, earn this slot.

support_spans: seizure-like behavior: episodes of head jerking with eye fluttering without tongue biting; remained conversant; benign neurologic examination.
contradict_spans: psychotic signs: mouthing words and seemingly responding to internal stimuli; thought blocking; reported auditory hallucinations.
concepts.why: The patient's seizure-like behavior with a benign neurologic examination earns this slot.
